title: Kafka Basics
chunks: Kafka partitions split a topic across brokers; each partition is an ordered append-only log.
Consumer groups track a committed offset per partition so consumers resume where they left off.
ISR (in-sync replicas) and the high-watermark control durability and what consumers can read.

title: Redis Caching
chunks: Redis is an in-memory key-value store used as a cache.
Eviction policies like LRU and LFU decide which keys to drop when maxmemory is hit; TTL expires keys.
Persistence options are RDB snapshots and the AOF append-only file.

title: PostgreSQL Internals
chunks: PostgreSQL uses MVCC so readers never block writers; each row version carries xmin/xmax.
VACUUM reclaims dead tuples left behind by MVCC and updates the visibility map.
The query planner chooses between sequential scans and index scans by cost.

title: Docker Containers
chunks: A Docker image is built from a Dockerfile as a stack of read-only layers.
Containers add a writable layer on top of the image at runtime.
Volumes persist data outside the container's writable layer.

title: Kubernetes Workloads
chunks: A Pod is the smallest deployable unit; a Deployment manages replica sets of Pods.
The scheduler places Pods onto nodes based on resource requests and constraints.
A Service gives a stable virtual IP and load-balances across matching Pods.

title: TLS Handshake
chunks: The TLS handshake negotiates a cipher suite and authenticates the server via its certificate.
Certificates chain to a trusted certificate authority; the client verifies the signature.
Session keys derived during the handshake encrypt the subsequent application data.

title: OAuth 2.0
chunks: The OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow exchanges a short-lived code for an access token.
Scopes limit what the access token can do; refresh tokens obtain new access tokens.
PKCE protects the authorization code flow for public clients without a client secret.

title: Git Workflow
chunks: Git branches are movable pointers to commits; merging combines two branch histories.
Rebase replays commits onto a new base for a linear history instead of a merge commit.
A worktree checks out an additional branch into a separate directory of the same repo.
